thread:
jess-support: Customer (org: acme-inc) reports UI shows monthly credits refilled at 00:00 local, but their service continues to get 429s when using a long-lived API token. They say it started immediately after the refill window. Attaching basic repro.

matt-ops: thanks — can you paste the curl and the exact 429 response headers?

jess-support: here's minimal repro: \n```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_longtoken123' \
  'https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate'
```
Response headers snippet: \n```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests\nX-RateLimit-Limit: 1000000\nX-RateLimit-Remaining: 0\nX-RateLimit-Reset: 1768904300\nRetry-After: 60\n```
Body: {"error":"quota_exhausted","message":"monthly credits exhausted"}

kevin-billing: UI shows org monthly bucket +1,200,000 tokens at 2026-02-09T00:00:00-08:00 for acme-inc. Billing confirms refill executed. So looks like a mismatch between billing state and enforcement.

sarah-infra: interesting — long-lived tokens are cached at edge quota layer for performance. Cache TTL is 300s by default. If the refill happened and the cache wasn't invalidated, enforcement could still see old value. Can you confirm token was used continuously (long sessions) across the rollover?

jess-support: customer says their microservice kept using same token without restart. They hit 429s immediately; UI showed refilled. They tried creating a new keyed token and that call worked.

matt-ops: that is a good signal. If new tokens observe updated quota and old tokens still 429, it's stale edge cache. Can you get the full header X-Quota-Cache: ? from a failing request? We usually add a header like X-Quota-Cache: miss|hit|stale.

jess-support: added what we got from logs: \n```
X-Quota-Cache: hit,ttl=240,ver=2026020900\nX-Edge-Node: edge-ia-12\n```

sarah-infra: confirms: hit on edge node edge-ia-12 with old version tag. Cache ver didn't update because the cache invalidation event didn't propagate — we had transient redis pubsub partitions during the refill window (noise from a config rollout). I can pull edge logs and force invalidation for that key.

infra-bot: cache-invalidator: queued purge for token sk_live_longtoken123 on edge-ia-12

matt-ops: after purge, customer should retry. Also we should instruct them that rotating the token is a safe immediate workaround.

jess-support: told customer to rotate the token — they did and calls succeeded. They asked for root cause and will need a postmortem for SLA impact.

kevin-billing: note for billing: even though UI/top-up executed, enforcement layer should never be out-of-sync more than TTL. But here TTL persisted because invalidation messages were dropped for ~7s during the pubsub blip. That allowed clients that never rotated tokens to see stale state for up to TTL (300s).

sarah-infra: action items: 1) increase pubsub retry and ack logic to avoid dropped invalidation messages, 2) add a short secondary check for monthly refills at enforcement time for long-lived tokens (cheap minimum sanity check), 3) set cache TTL for quota entries to max 60s for refill windows. I'll open infra tickets.

jess-support: customer satisfied with token rotation workaround and requested ETA for infra fixes.

matt-ops: ETA: will push quick fix (retry bump + metrics) within 48h, and a config change to TTL within 7 days. We'll follow up in thread once infra tickets created.

sarah-infra: created infra ticket INFRA-4821 and added chase for pubsub diagnostics. Also updated incident timeline and root-cause notes.

jess-support: closing loop with customer. Follow-up note: recommended they handle token rotation on refill as a defensive pattern until infra changes land. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: INFRA-4821 created by sarah-infra — https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-4821\n
